30 Minutes to Productive

From one line in a terminal to an AI skill you built yourself, that gives the same answer every time and goes wherever you go.

Before the session: do step 1 at your desk if you can. Forty sign-ins from one room at once can make GitHub slow down sign-in.
1

Install and sign in

0 to 5 min

Mac: open Terminal and paste:

curl -fsSL https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/install.sh | bash

Windows: open PowerShell and paste:

irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/aibast-agents-library/main/install.ps1 | iex

The chat opens in your browser. Click Sign in with GitHub and enter the code it shows. You need GitHub Copilot access.

2

Talk to it

5 to 8 min

Type: "What can you do?" It answers using the skills in its agents folder. Each skill is one file.

3

Use a real skill from the library

8 to 13 min

Pick a solution in the library. Every one has an agent file. Download it into your Brainstem's agents folder. For example, the First-Time Fix agent:

curl -fsSL -o ~/.brainstem/src/rapp_brainstem/agents/first_time_fix_agent.py https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/aibast-agents-library/main/agents/%40aibast-agents-library/telecom_media_gaming_stacks/first_time_fix_stack/first_time_fix_agent.py

Windows (PowerShell):

iwr https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/aibast-agents-library/main/agents/%40aibast-agents-library/telecom_media_gaming_stacks/first_time_fix_stack/first_time_fix_agent.py -OutFile "$env:USERPROFILE\.brainstem\src\rapp_brainstem\agents\first_time_fix_agent.py"

No restart. On the next message, ask: "The customer on Alder Grove Service keeps dropping. What guided fix should I walk them through right now?" It answers from the sample records inside that one file.

4

See why one file matters

13 to 18 min

Most AI tools hand you a pile of parts: a model, a harness, a loop, skill files, connectors. You become the glue. An agent.py is the whole thing in one file: what it does, what it needs, the steps, and its sample data. The Brainstem is the loop that runs it.

Prove it runs anywhere. Copy any agent file and basic_agent.py from your agents folder into an empty folder, swap files with your neighbour, and each run:

python3 -c "import hashlib; from weather_agent import WeatherAgent; a = WeatherAgent().perform(city='Seattle'); print(a); print(hashlib.sha256(a.encode()).hexdigest()[:12])"

The weather agent comes from the 5-minute tutorial. Same file, same input, same fingerprint on both machines. You checked instead of trusting. Any folder with those two files is a Brainstem.

5

Build your own skill

18 to 26 min

Think of a small task from your week: tidy meeting notes, check a document for missing fields, turn a list into a table. In the chat, type:

Learn a new skill: given a list of meeting action items as text, return them as a checklist grouped by owner, with any item that has no owner under Unassigned.

It writes the file and loads it. The first version is a starter: open the file and you will see its steps are a placeholder. Hand the file to GitHub Copilot with:

Make perform() do the real steps in code, with no AI calls, so the same input always gives the same output. Keep the class, the name and the metadata.

Save it back into agents and try it in the chat. If something is wrong, tell Copilot exactly what you typed and what came back. One round is usually enough. Ask the same thing twice: same answer both times.

6

Take it with you

26 to 30 min

Your skill is a file you own. Email it, keep it in a repo, hand it to a teammate. It works in their Brainstem the moment it lands in agents.

When a skill proves itself, the library shows the path to Copilot Studio and Microsoft 365 for real users. The file stays the original; every platform version is made from it.

You are productive

You installed it, used a real skill, proved it runs anywhere, and built one of your own.
